If your part looks wider in photos, your ponytail feels thinner, or there’s more hair in the shower drain than there used to be, you’ve probably come across pumpkin seed oil. It’s one of the most talked-about natural options for women’s thinning hair, and for good reason: it’s rich in plant sterols that help block DHT, the hormone behind female pattern thinning.

The problem is that “pumpkin seed oil serum” on a label can mean very different things. Some are mostly water, silicones and fragrance with a splash of oil. Some use refined, heat-treated oil that has lost the very compounds that matter. Others are so heavy they sit on the hair instead of the scalp.

So we looked at the four types of pumpkin seed oil serum women are most likely to come across, and judged them on the five things that decide whether a serum is worth your money.

settings.title: The short version
settings.text: Pumpkin seed oil only helps if it reaches your scalp with its sterols intact, alongside something that supports the growth phase, in a formula light enough to use every night. Of the four types we compared, Elaren was the only one that does all three, and it comes with a 30-day money-back guarantee.

settings.title: 5 Things That Separate a Serum That Works From One That Doesn’t
settings.subtitle: Before you compare prices, compare these.

settings.title: Cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil
settings.text: Heat and solvents strip out the phytosterols, zinc and vitamin E that make pumpkin seed oil worth using. Cold-pressed oil keeps them intact, and you can see it in the deep green-gold colour.

settings.title: A supporting active, not just oil
settings.text: Pumpkin seed oil works on DHT. Pairing it with caffeine, one of the most-studied topical actives for hair, also supports the growth phase of the follicle.

settings.title: No filler
settings.text: Water, mineral oil and silicones bulk out a bottle and make hair look shiny, but do nothing for the follicle. Every drop should be doing a job.

settings.title: Light enough to use every night
settings.text: Regrowth comes from consistency. A serum that leaves your hair greasy or flat is a serum you’ll stop using by week three.

settings.title: Honest research and a real guarantee
settings.text: Look for a brand that cites studies done on women, says exactly what was studied, and stands behind results with a money-back guarantee.

settings.text: Why Elaren Came Out on Top

Elaren was formulated for the way women’s hair thins after 35, when falling oestrogen lets DHT gain the upper hand and the follicles along the part and crown slowly shrink.

It starts with cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil, which keeps its phytosterols (beta-sitosterol and delta-7-sterine), zinc and vitamin E intact. Those sterols help inhibit 5-alpha-reductase, the enzyme that turns testosterone into DHT. Then it adds a Caffeine Complex, which counteracts DHT’s effect on the follicle and helps extend the growth phase.

Nothing else in the bottle is filler: no water, no mineral oil, no silicones. It sinks in overnight without a greasy residue, and it works on coils, curls, waves and straight hair, under wigs and braids.
“My scalp feels noticeably healthier, and it sinks in without that heavy, greasy feeling.”
What the research says

In a 3-month randomised trial of 60 women with female pattern hair loss, those who applied pumpkin seed oil to the scalp had fewer fine, miniaturised hairs and more new regrowing hairs.* The other half used 5% minoxidil foam, which did better overall, but pumpkin seed oil still produced measurable improvement on its own, without a drug.

In laboratory research on hair follicles from women’s scalps, caffeine lengthened the growth phase and increased hair-shaft growth, and women’s follicles proved especially responsive to it.*

settings.text: How to Use It, and What to Expect

Every night, two minutes. Part your hair and apply a few drops directly to the scalp where it’s thinning: your part, crown, temples or edges. Massage in with your fingertips for 60 seconds, then leave it in overnight and wash as normal in the morning.

Be patient, hair grows in cycles. Most women notice less hair in the brush and the shower drain within the first 2–4 weeks, and fuller-looking hair by day 30. Fine new baby hairs along the hairline and part usually show up around month 2 or 3, and density keeps building the longer you stay consistent.

settings.title: Our tip
settings.text: Don’t stop at week three. Consistency is the whole secret, which is why most women start with a 3-month supply.

settings.question: How is Elaren different from other pumpkin seed oil serums?
settings.answer: Most serums use refined pumpkin seed oil diluted with water, mineral oil or silicones. Elaren uses cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil, so its DHT-blocking sterols, zinc and vitamin E stay intact, and adds a Caffeine Complex to support the growth phase. There is no filler in the bottle, and it is light enough to use every night.

settings.question: How soon will I see results?
settings.answer: Hair grows in cycles, so give it a full 30 days of nightly use. Most customers notice less shedding in the first weeks and fuller-looking hair around day 30, with new baby hairs along the part and hairline in the months after. Consistency matters more than anything: two minutes a night, every night.

settings.question: How do I use it?
settings.answer: Part dry or towel-dried hair, apply a few drops directly to the scalp where you are thinning (the part, crown, temples or hairline) and massage in for about 60 seconds to get the blood flowing. Leave it in overnight and wash as normal in the morning. One tube is a one-month supply.

settings.question: Will it make my hair greasy?
settings.answer: No. The oil is lightweight and goes on the scalp, not the lengths, so it absorbs while you sleep. Customers with fine hair and with alopecia tell us it does not feel greasy once applied, and your normal morning wash takes care of the rest.

settings.question: Which kinds of hair loss does it help with?
settings.answer: It was made for the ways women’s hair thins after 35: female pattern thinning at the part and crown, postpartum and menopausal shedding, traction and breakage along the edges, and stress shedding. Pumpkin seed oil targets DHT at the follicle while the Caffeine Complex wakes dormant follicles. It is a cosmetic scalp treatment, not a medicine, so it cannot cure medical conditions such as alopecia areata, though many customers use it to support the hair they have.

settings.question: Is it safe? Can I use it with other treatments?
settings.answer: The formula is drug-free and hormone-free: cold-pressed pumpkin seed oil, caffeine and plant-based actives, no minoxidil. Most women can use it alongside their usual products. If you are pregnant, breastfeeding or under medical treatment for hair loss, check with your doctor first.
